project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer: Develop and test a vendor-independent platform for distribution operators to control their networks and use local flexibility.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer: Design and test a vendor-independent distribution management platform. Address network control, distributed resources, forecasting, analytical displays, interoperability and security. Use or develop open-source modules where possible.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer: Local grid operators need to manage more distributed generation and demand flexibility while keeping their network and the transmission grid coordinated.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer: Deliver a distribution platform and a vendor-independent architecture. Provide an operations manual, best practices and a list of remaining development needs.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Make local networks more controllable and reliable. Operators should be better able to manage congestion and coordinate with neighbouring and higher-voltage networks.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer: Give other distribution operators practical instructions and best practices. Describe credible cooperation with the transmission control-room project and participate in BRIDGE (the European network for sharing smart-grid, storage and digital energy results).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: The proposal needs at least three independent funded partners and is expected to bring together at least five relevant organisations. At least one must be established in a European Union Member State. The other two must be established in different Member States or countries associated with Horizon Europe (countries formally participating in the European research programme). The topic expects three distribution operators and two universities or research organisations.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer: The project is expected to include at least three distribution operators and two universities or research organisations. It encourages a supplier and at least one connected transmission operator.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · Consortium composition

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer: Meet the expected partner profile at project level. The proposal should explain how the work links to the separately funded transmission control-room project.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: The group appoints a funded partner to lead the work on distribution management platforms and represent it to the funder.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer: TenneT could coordinate the project if it can fill the encouraged adjacent transmission-operator role and validate an interface with a distribution partner. The applicants choose their coordinator (the funded partner that represents the group to the funder).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer: TenneT could take part in distribution management platforms without receiving a grant. As an associated partner (an organisation that works without a grant), it could fill the encouraged adjacent transmission-operator role and validate an interface with a distribution partner. It would cover its own costs and would not count towards the minimum number of funded partners.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 5, 11–13 · B — Eligibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · Consortium roles, Coordinator and Associated partners

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer: TenneT can receive up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow) for qualifying work. The Dutch entity could fill the encouraged adjacent transmission-operator role and validate an interface with a distribution partner. Budget at least 30% of those costs from other resources. The topic excludes organisations directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established there.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer: TenneT could design and test the transmission interface with an adjoining distribution operator. It could validate whether forecasts and flexibility activations remain useful across both networks.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: Design and test innovative platforms and processes. The call expects modern tools such as digital twins (virtual network models) and open-source modules where possible.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: The innovation is in software architecture, forecasts, analytical tools and operating processes for flexible distribution grids.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Design the platform, test how it handles distributed resources and validate it across at least two pilots in different eligible countries.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 6–8 (technology readiness level: from demonstration in relevant conditions to a complete, qualified system) by project end. The call allows work to start at any maturity level.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Specific conditions

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: Test the platform at a minimum of two pilots in different eligible countries. Partners can divide the work between the pilots as long as the project meets the collaboration profile overall.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: Connect the platform to other distribution operators, transmission operators and local resources such as controllable demand or generation. Explain how the project will work with the separately funded transmission control-room project.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: Test whether the platform improves grid control, forecasting, congestion management and the use of distributed resources.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?
cards.answer: At least three distribution system operators are expected to take part. The call encourages a connected transmission operator and a technology supplier so both interfaces can be tested.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer: The software should build in protection from the design stage and include safeguards against cyber threats. Protect the operator-to-operator and distributed-device data exchanges.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Scope

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 28.5 million for distribution management platforms. It expects 3 awards.
- Grant request: Around EUR 9.5 million per project. Different requests are eligible.
- Funding form: Budget-based grant (paid using approved costs or rates for the funded work).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 176–178 · Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · p. 48 · Overview of this call
Advanced Distribution Management Systems (ADSM) for more efficient and flexible distribution grids · Budget overview
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards distribution management platforms.
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Plan the budget for distribution management platforms using the cost categories allowed by the grant. The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) specifies how those costs can be claimed.
- Eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow): Personnel, subcontracting and purchases are principal categories.
- Overheads and value added tax (tax on purchases): The 25% indirect-cost rate (overheads such as general office expenses) excludes subcontracting, third-party support and categories already including indirect costs.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount and Budget categories and cost eligibility rules

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Plan cash flow for distribution management platforms around the initial advance and later payments.
- Payment model: Pre-financing (an advance at the start of the grant) usually precedes periodic payments and the final balance.
- Retention or guarantee: The mutual insurance mechanism (a common fund covering grant recovery risks) deducts 5–8% of the maximum grant from pre-financing.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 33 · Reporting & payment arrangements

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for distribution management platforms through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 1 December 2027, 17:00 Brussels time. Submit Part A (online administration form) and Part B (technical proposal) with a 40-page limit.
- Opening: 4 August 2027.
cards.sources:

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for distribution management platforms.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
The Commission’s timetable for assessing and contracting distribution management platforms is indicative.
- Expected invitation or assessment result: Around five months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules): Around eight months from the full-proposal deadline.
- Conditions before starting: The beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) must conclude a written consortium agreement (the partners’ written agreement on how the project will run).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
Use the portal’s forms to submit the proposal and supporting documents for distribution management platforms.
- Application form: Complete online Part A and upload technical Part B and applicable annexes.
- Registration: Beneficiaries (organisations formally responsible for funded work) and affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to funded partners) need a participant identification code before submission.
- Partner documents: The coordinator confirms its authority to act for the applicant group at submission. Participants sign declarations of honour (signed confirmations of eligibility and other requirements) before grant signature.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · Entities eligible to participate

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Distribution management platforms proposals compete on research quality, impact and the quality of the delivery plan.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence, impact, and quality and efficiency of implementation.
- Thresholds: At least 3/5 on each criterion and 10/15 overall.
- Ranking rules: Ties first favour uncovered topic aspects. The next criteria are impact then excellence.
- Weighting: The impact score (the score for what the project is expected to achieve) has a 1.5 multiplier for ranking.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 28–29 · Evaluation procedure and ranking

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Explain how the distribution-management project can work with the separately funded transmission control-room project.
- Conditional — Adjacent-network coordination: Proposals are expected to set out credible collaboration with a funded transmission system operator control-room project under the separate control-room call.
- Conditional — Satellite data or services: Use Copernicus for Earth observation and/or Galileo or the European Geostationary Navigation Overlay Service for satellite positioning, navigation or timing where the proposal uses the covered services.
- Conditional — China control: Entities directly or indirectly controlled by China or an entity established there are ineligible.
